alternatives.mechanism: Implement a tolerant parser that first attempts to detect the file format (JSON, YAML, CSV, or simple line‑based) and then uses a generic data model; for any blocked task lacking a "responsible" field, insert a placeholder like "<no owner>" and emit a warning.
addresses_issues: Parsing of the task list may fail for formats not explicitly supported
Assumes every blocked task has a responsible field
tradeoffs: Adds complexity to the codebase and increases binary size
Placeholder may hide data‑quality problems, requiring users to monitor warnings
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Formato‑agnóstico com fallback automático e preenchimento de campos ausentes

alternatives.mechanism: Restrict the tool to a single, well‑defined format (e.g., JSON) and provide a concise schema; include a validation step that reports missing "responsible" fields and skips those tasks rather than crashing.
addresses_issues: Parsing of the task list may fail for formats not explicitly supported
Assumes every blocked task has a responsible field
tradeoffs: Limits usability to users who can produce the exact format
Tasks without a responsible field are omitted, potentially losing information
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Abordagem de "formato único" com validação estrita para garantir robustez

alternatives.mechanism: Design a plugin‑based architecture where core logic loads a parser plugin supplied by the user (e.g., via a simple script); the core also treats missing "responsible" fields as optional and displays "Unassigned" when absent.
addresses_issues: Parsing of the task list may fail for formats not explicitly supported
Assumes every blocked task has a responsible field
tradeoffs: Requires users to write or install plugins, raising the entry barrier
Runtime overhead of dynamic loading and potential security considerations
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Extensibilidade via plugins que permitem suporte a novos formatos e tratamento flexível de campos ausentes
